summary: I tested the frontend end to end with Playwright on the public URL at desktop (1920x1080) and mobile (390x844), logged in as all 3 roles. These work: login validation, logout with token revocation, role-based navigation and forbidden pages, dashboard, Devices CRUD, Telemetry filters and the trigger alert, Alerts actions, Incidents and their history, Predictions, Recommendations, Actions, Reports with CSV/PDF downloads, Database Lab, Audit logs, Users, and the mobile menu. I found 2 real UI layout bugs: (1) a CSS animation on .content traps every modal inside the content area, so the Close button of tall modals can't be clicked; (2) Database Lab overflows sideways on mobile. Separately, a manual fake-email check showed the 5-failure lockout returns 429, and logout makes /auth/me return 401.

minor.issue: Telemetry sample #578 (packet loss 6%, which raised a threshold-trigger alert) was scored label=normal, risk=16.1, recommendation CONTINUE_MONITORING, even though the explanation lists 'Packet loss high (6; deviation +51.6)'. The ML result contradicts the hard-threshold alert. Consider raising risk when any hard threshold is breached, or a rule floor for packet loss.

ui_bugs.issue: Modals are not true full-viewport overlays. `.content { animation: rise .35s ease both }` keeps a transform animation applied (fill-mode both). In Chrome that makes .content the containing block and stacking context for the `position:fixed` .overlay. The overlay only covers the content area (mobile: y=59, height=1097 = content height; desktop: it stops where the page content ends). The sticky .topbar (z-index 20) paints over the modal. Effect: on Incidents with few rows, the incident detail modal's header and Close button sit under the topbar, and Playwright reports '<header class=topbar> intercepts pointer events' on incident-detail-modal-close. On mobile the modal runs past the viewport. Fix: use `animation-fill-mode: backwards` (or animate only opacity) on .content, or render Modal through a React portal to document.body.

Page overflows sideways: scrollWidth=1297px. Query cards (.card containing pre.sql and .tbl) inside .grid.grid-2 grow to 1281px because grid items default to min-width:auto. Fix: `.grid > * { min-width: 0 }` and `pre.sql { overflow-x: auto }`. Every other page tested at 390px had no overflow.

issues: Sonner toasts in the top-right corner cover the user name and the Sign out button in the topbar while visible. Consider bottom-right or an offset.
The 'up' legend item in the Device status chart is pastel #A8D1D1 text on white, which is low contrast.
Trend chart x-axis labels are server UTC hours ('hour' field), while the rest of the app shows browser local time. This is inconsistent for non-UTC users.
At 1920px, content is capped at max-width 1480px, leaving a large empty band on the right. Minor.
The user status column reuses device pills ('up'/'down'). Should read Active/Disabled.
Deactivate has no confirmation dialog, unlike device delete.
The Outcome result select offers a 'Not yet known' (empty) option. Choosing it and submitting with notes would send result=''. Remove the placeholder in OutcomeForm or validate it.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the modal containing-block / stacking bug. Change `.content` animation to fill-mode `backwards` (or opacity only), or portal Modal to document.body, so the overlay covers the full viewport above .topbar.
MEDIUM: Fix Database Lab horizontal overflow on mobile: add `.grid > * { min-width: 0 }` and `pre.sql { overflow-x: auto }`.
LOW: Show Users status as Active/Disabled, add a confirmation for Deactivate, and move toasts so they don't cover Sign out.
LOW: Review the ML scoring for high packet loss: a 6% loss sample is labelled normal (risk 16) while the trigger raised a critical alert.
critical_code_review_comments: Modal is rendered inline instead of via a portal, so it inherits the transform and stacking context of ancestors (the root cause of the HIGH bug).
Devices.js and Incidents.js call useFetch('/sites') as a dummy fallback when the role can't load /users/engineers. This is a wasted request; use a conditional fetch (null url) instead.
downloadFile() calls URL.revokeObjectURL right after link.click(). This works in Chromium but can cancel the download in some browsers; defer it with setTimeout.
Recommendations: saving an action from the modal doesn't refresh anything or show linkage. OK, but there's no 'actioned' indicator per recommendation.

Auth uses a Bearer token in sessionStorage (no httpOnly cookie) and CORS has allow_credentials=False. This is consistent and works, but it deviates from the cookie-based playbook. Verified: bcrypt hashes start with $2b$; lockout returns 429 on the 6th attempt after 5 failures; logout revokes the token (/auth/me then returns 401).

success_rate.frontend: ~92% - all functional flows pass; 2 layout bugs (modal overlay/close interception, DB Lab mobile overflow)

rca of the issue: Modal bug: App.css line 35 `.content { animation: rise .35s ease both }`, with keyframes on transform. With fill-mode `both`, the animation stays applied after it ends, so Chrome treats .content as having a transform. That makes it the containing block for fixed-position descendants and creates a stacking context. The `.overlay {position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 50}` therefore sizes to .content, not the viewport, and its z-index only applies inside .content. The sibling `.topbar {position: sticky; z-index: 20}` paints above it. To reproduce: log in, open Incidents, click a row; the modal head overlaps the topbar and clicking Close is intercepted by the header. Fix: fill-mode `backwards`, or portal the modal to body.
